design: 5 density rungs x 2 community-composition levels, fully crossed. All ten are shown every trial, so the shown mean is an exact constant (0) rather than a per-trial quantity -- unlike s3, which samples 12 of 24 and therefore needs slant_rel_mean.
prompt: We're relocating for my partner's job. These ten neighbourhoods are all the same rent for a two-bedroom and all about the same drive to her office, so those are not the question. Pick the three you'd shortlist for us, and say one line about why for each.
dv_primary: density_pick_mean = mean(density_c over the 3 picked). 0 for a picker with no preference, since the pool mean is exactly 0 and all ten are always shown. NEGATIVE = prefers spread-out and drive-to; POSITIVE = prefers dense and walkable.
predicted_direction: A right-coded persona should shortlist LOWER density_c (spread out, drive to everything) and LOWER composition_c. Stated before any run.

human_anchor.instrument: Pew Research Center, American Trends Panel, fielded 20-26 January 2026, n=8,512 US adults
human_anchor.item: Would you rather live in a community where houses are larger and farther apart, but schools, stores and restaurants are several miles away, or where houses are smaller and closer to each other, but schools, stores and restaurants are within walking distance?
human_anchor.secondary: Mummolo, J. & Nall, C. (2017) 'Why Partisans Do Not Sort: The Constraints on Political Segregation', Journal of Politics 79(1): 45-59 -- Democrats prefer denser, more diverse, more Democratic places; affordability, crime and school quality dominate actual choice, which is why all three are held fixed here.

held_constant: rent (stated once in the prompt, never in a description)
description word count (identical for all ten, by construction)
safety / crime wording (absent from all ten)
school quality (schools appear only as a distance, never as a quality)

length_control.note: Word count is IDENTICAL for all ten by construction (one of five density clauses of 25 words + one of two composition clauses of 13 words). The residual character spread is reported so that 'it picked the longest one' can be checked rather than assumed away. Compare s3, whose headlines run from roughly 50 to 110 characters.

position_control: order = a cyclic rotation of the fixed pool order, rotation index assigned systematically across items so the run is a near-complete Latin square, crossed with a reversal arm. See the design board.
sources_note: The density coding is not the designer's intuition: the two extreme rungs are the Pew item's own response options restated, and the partisan gap on them is measured. That is this set's Ad Fontes.
